prerequisites.title: X developer account
prerequisites.detail: Sign in at console.x.com with an X account, accept the Developer Agreement and Policy, and describe how you will use the API.

prerequisites.title: Funded credits
prerequisites.detail: The X API is pay-per-usage, and you buy credits upfront. Prices are subject to change.

prerequisites.title: An X representative
prerequisites.detail: Raising Ads API access or the token limit goes through your X representative.

steps.title: Create developer account
steps.detail: Sign in at console.x.com, accept the agreement, and describe your use case clearly and specifically.
steps.done_when: The Developer Console dashboard is available.

steps.title: Draft app name and use case
steps.detail: Write a specific app description and use case that matches the access you need.

steps.title: Create app and save credentials
steps.detail: Create the app, then copy the Client ID and Secret immediately. They are shown once.
steps.done_when: Client ID and Secret are stored securely.

steps.title: Buy credits and set spend cap
steps.detail: Purchase credits and optionally set a per-cycle spending limit, since requests are blocked once it is reached.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create a custom auth config for the X toolkit with your Client ID and Secret. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard into the X app settings.
steps.done_when: A test user connects an account.

steps.title: Request Standard Access
steps.detail: Contact your X representative to apply for Standard Access or a higher token limit.

steps.title: Wait for X response
steps.detail: Reported waits range from immediate to several days, with no published SLA. One 2020 report took over a month and ended in rejection.

traps.title: Credentials shown only once
traps.detail: Losing them forces a regeneration, which invalidates the old ones.

traps.title: Costs are separate from rate limits
traps.detail: You can incur usage costs while within rate limits. Pay-per-usage plans cap Post reads at 3 million per monthly billing cycle.

traps.title: Vague use case gets rejected
traps.detail: Reported rejection causes are a vague use-case description or a request that does not match the access tier.

traps.title: Ads token cap and fixed rate limits
traps.detail: Older Ads apps may be limited to 5 user tokens, and X does not raise Ads rate limits.

traps.title: Pricing differs by endpoint
traps.detail: The lower Owned Read price only applies to your own app owner's data, not your end users' data.

blockers.what_it_means: The use case was reportedly too vague or did not match the requested tier.
blockers.what_to_do: Resubmit with a specific, accurate use-case description.

blockers.symptom: Ads endpoints unavailable or token limit reached
blockers.what_it_means: The app is limited to certain app-level permissions or a user token cap.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask your X representative for Standard Access or a higher token limit.

blockers.what_it_means: The spending limit you set was reached.
blockers.what_to_do: Raise the limit or wait for the next billing cycle.
